localResults.item: PACKAGE THE ALIGNMENT GATE as a standalone tool (scratchpad/ship/alignment_gate/)
localResults.verified_basis: (1) Premise CONFIRMED: verify_alignment_out.json ref medians recomputed this session = ours 68.07 deg (0/8 within 30), published 13.11 deg (7/9 within 30) — consistent with the corrected 68.1/13.1 pair and identical to the primary artifacts pherc0813_mesh_alignment.json (68.074) and published_mesh_alignment.json (13.115); the file's two independent estimators (forward-diff, PCA) agree with those medians within ~2 deg. (2) The packaged code reproduces the calibration EXACTLY on real data: all 8 PHerc0813 mesh normals and angles-vs-stored-sheet-normals match the artifact to 0.0000 deg; full end-to-end packaged method (mesh normal + structure-tensor sheet normal) on the 9 published meshes with their 256^3 calibration cubes reproduces every angle to 0.0000 deg (median 13.11, 7/9 within 30). (3) Cube size premise checked, not assumed: calibration cubes measured as 256^3 uint8 on disk, so the gate default is --cube 256 (my initial 160 inference from n_blocks=125 was wrong — that count came from the block=48 verify run — caught and fixed). (4) Self-test on synthetic known-orientation data passes 4/4: aligned plane 0.0 ALIGNED, aligned+(-1 sentinels) 0.0 ALIGNED (sentinel regression: fixed mask excludes exactly the -1 vertices, old zero-mask catches none; erosion bars sentinel-adjacent vertices), 45-deg plane 45.0 REJECT, orthogonal plane 90.0 REJECT; CLI exit codes verified (1 on reject, 3 on missing volume and on usage error, 0 on help/pass). (5) npy, 3D-tif-stack, and slice-directory volume readers all tested and give identical results.

README.md — what the gate catches (surfaces that look healthy — right area, ~0.9999 validity fill, non-zero DN — while tracking no lamella), the PHerc0813 case (median 68.1, 0/8 within 30, all 8 rejected, worse than random 60), calibration table, method spec with the sentinel-fix rationale, usage, exit codes, borderline-result guidance.
localResults.numbers: Premise: ref medians 68.07/13.11 deg, within-30 0/8 and 7/9 (matches 68.1/13.1). Cross-validation on real data: max deviation from calibration artifacts 0.0000 deg over 8 ours (mesh-normal + angle) and 9 published (full end-to-end with 256^3 cubes; packaged median 13.11, 7/9 within 30). Calibration cubes: 256^3 uint8 (measured; gate default --cube 256 = 8^3 blocks of 32). Self-test: aligned 0.0 ALIGNED, aligned_sentinel 0.0 ALIGNED, oblique45 45.0 REJECT, orthogonal 90.0 REJECT; buggy zero-mask vs fixed on sentinel mesh: mask catches 0 of 741 sentinels vs all 741; exit codes 1/3/3/0 as documented.
localResults.honest_limits: The volume-window path (extracting a 256^3 window from a whole volume at the mesh centroid) was validated only on synthetic data; the real-data calibration reproduction used the pre-extracted 256^3 cubes, which were centred at seed sites rather than mesh centroids — on real whole-scroll volumes a centroid-centred window may differ slightly from the seed-site cubes, though the structure-tensor statistic is an average over 512 blocks and both self-test and calibration agree wherever both are testable. The zarr reader is written but untested (no zarr test data; other three readers tested and identical). Gate default measures orientation at one site per mesh (as calibrated); a mesh aligned at its centroid but drifting elsewhere needs --split > 1, whose per-tile behaviour was tested on synthetic data only. On the synthetic flat-plane sentinel mesh the old zero-mask bug only shifts the normal by 1.22 deg (the real-data damage came from ~50%-invalid curved meshes), so the regression test asserts on the mask/erosion behaviour, which is exact, not on a large angle delta. Published population contains two genuine >30 rejects (47.5, 59.2 deg), so even good pipelines are not 9/9 — the gate flags patches, it does not certify pipelines.
localResults.problems: Two of my own inferences failed triple-checking and were fixed before shipping: (a) I initially defaulted the window to 160^3 by misreading n_blocks=125 from the block=48 verify run; the calibration cubes are actually 256^3 (measured on disk), default corrected to 256. (b) SystemExit("msg") exits 1 and argparse usage errors exit 2 (colliding with INDETERMINATE), so the documented bad-input=3 contract required an explicit remap, now tested. Also, the Bash heredoc write of the main script was mangled by the shell wrapper on the first attempt (fell back to the Write tool), and one non-ASCII identifier slipped into selftest.py and was replaced. published_mesh_alignment.json stores no normals (different schema from the PHerc0813 artifact), so the published-side validation was done by re-running the full method against the cached cubes instead of comparing stored normals — arguably a stronger check.

localResults.item: NULL-SCALING METHODS RESULT (CPU-only, local data): premise reproduction, effective sample size of the rigid-shift null, one corrected null, and the corrected null applied to the corpus screen's "0 of 71 pass" flagship negative.
localResults.verified_basis: A stopped prior run had completed ns1-ns3 and one ns4 map; I did not trust it: ns1 was re-run (bit-identical), ns2's entire 400-draw ensemble was REGENERATED from scratch with the cache moved aside (draw matrices and JSON bit-identical), ns3 re-run (bit-identical). The corpus gate decomposition was recomputed independently from raw corpus_analysis_v2.json before ns4a's version was consulted (both agree: 0/71 pass all gates, 0/71 pass the four null-free gates, gate_fwd_rev passes 0/71, min r 0.2215 vs <0.2). Every re-null run asserts the observed prominence equals the stored screen value (e.g. 58.062==58.062) before counting a single draw, and uses the screen's own prep/score/joint_permute module, not a reimplementation. The tile-64 path was validated on 00215 (fresh-seed 50-perm p 0.059 vs stored 200-perm p 0.0398).
localResults.numbers: PREMISE (reproduced, not killed): Frag1 obs +1914.07 on 2560 tiles, 40-draw null sd 2755.28 (all 40 draws reproduce to <0.02); heavy tail: worst draw -12,833 vs IQR [-992,+1334], excess kurtosis +9.84, one draw = 55.3% of null variance; sd*sqrt(n) spans 57,650..146,740 across Frag1 slabs (2.55x) and 59,173..139,407 across plates (2.36x). ESS: converged 400-draw sd 2091.9 (the committed 2755.3 is a +1.6 SE fluctuation; SE of a 40-draw sd = 406 = 19.4%); DEFF 2.0, n_eff 566 vs nominal 2560 (22%, a 4.5x overcount); null draws admit median 1400 tiles vs 2560 observed; null-field correlation: x 1/e at lag 3 tiles, y white beyond lag 1. CORRECTED NULL (2x8-tile block bootstrap, matched-n, 4000 reps): whole-plate sd 1227.6, z +1.56; seed-cv 0.43-0.69% vs rigid 40-draw estimator cv 6.5-23.6% per slab; slab constant spread 1.67x (40,202..67,321, whole-plate 62,112 inside it) vs rigid 2.80x at 400 draws; block-size sensitivity flat (1134..1256 for 1x4..4x12). Both directions: Frag1's G1 sd-gate FAIL is a 40-draw-estimator artifact (2091.9 and 1227.6 both < 2300), AND detection is not rescued (z +1.56 << 4). CORPUS PAYOFF: 0/71 pass the four null-free gates, so NO null correction can flip the verdict; measured at block 128 (>= measured L(0.1); 19/74 maps exceed the v2 tile of 64): passers went p .00498->.0588 (00260, strongest, L01_x=93>64), .0199->.0392 (00320), .0348->.1961 (00357), .0398->.0196 (00215) - 2 of 4 keep raw p<=.05 vs 3.55 expected by chance among 71; genuine-ruling control still passes (0/50 nulls >= obs, z +5.14 vs +16.26 at tile 64).
localResults.deliverable: "0 of 71 pass" SURVIVES - the flagship negative is NOT overconfident with respect to the null, and Ben can submit it as-is. It stands structurally (only 1 of 5 gates touches the null; 0/71 maps pass the other four; the fwd/rev gate alone kills everything at min r 0.2215 vs <0.2) and empirically (correlation-length-matched re-null leaves 2 chance-level significance passers out of an expected 3.55, all of which fail 2-4 null-free gates each). The only null defect found runs the OTHER way: the v2 tile-64 permutation is mildly anti-conservative on the 19/74 maps with correlation length > 64 px, and fixing it strips the strongest candidate (00260: p .005 -> .059) while the real-ruling control keeps passing - correcting the null strengthens the negative. Separately, the methods result itself: the rigid-shift null's 40-draw sd has n_eff 566 (not 2560) and 19% self-noise, which is why Frag1's G1 sd gate flipped on one draw; the block bootstrap at the measured correlation length is stable where the rigid null is not (seed-cv ~0.5% vs 6.5-23.6%; constant spread 1.67x vs 2.80x) and does not rescue detection (z +1.56). Writeup with all numbers: NULL_SCALING.md.
localResults.honest_limits: (1) Re-nulls use 50 perms (floor p=.0196) vs the screen's 200; adequate to call pass/fail at .05 but borderline calls (00320 at .0392) carry permutation noise. (2) Block 128 is below the passers' claimed 199-230-px periods, so a genuine ruling at those periods would survive the permutation - power was demonstrated only via the control at 0.98x its own period (a harder case). (3) The block bootstrap answers a matched-configuration question; it sits at median 0.65x the converged rigid ensemble because the rigid null also carries between-region nonstationarity (V1: single-null-field bootstrap median 1452 vs ensemble 2092). Which variance is 'the' null variance is a framing choice the writeup states explicitly rather than resolves; under EITHER framing Frag1's sd is < 2300 and z << 4. (4) The corrected-null z of +1.56 uses obs/boot_sd with a zero-centered null assumption; the rigid ensemble's own mean is -246, small against sd 2092. (5) Corpus conclusions rest on the v2 screen's stored gate booleans plus this session's recomputation from its raw JSON; the null-free gates themselves (fwd/rev threshold 0.2 etc.) were not re-audited - out of scope for a null-scaling item.
localResults.problems: None blocking. Two flags for the report phase: (a) if the null-free fwd/rev gate were ever loosened, the significance gate would become load-bearing and the tile-64 anti-conservatism (19/74 maps with L(0.1)>64) would matter - any future screen version should set the permutation tile at or above the per-map measured correlation length; (b) the G1 prereg gate thresholds a 40-draw sd of a heavy-tailed null (SE 19%) - a future prereg should use a converged ensemble or a robust dispersion statistic; Frag1's committed FAIL stands as committed but should not be interpreted as a property of the plate.

author.item: AUTHOR THE POD SCRIPT carrying both heavy experiments (detectability curve + hallucination audit) to RunPod
author.what_it_runs: One pod, ~27 inference passes, no torch.compile. EXP A: fetches Frag1 (65 uint16 TIFFs, 6.7 GB, 2.5 s sleeps, resumable, from the URL verified live today: dl.ash2txt.org/fragments/Frag1/PHercParis2Fr47.volpkg/working/54keV_exposed_surface, Content-Lengths 103571720/103571722 fingerprinted) + inklabels/mask PNGs (sha256-pinned to the laptop copies) + ink_9um seed42/step-075000 (public, size 138360039 asserted, config asserted mode=flat crop=(17,128,128) norm=robust_mad). Every layer's IFD is HAND-PARSED per file (both byte orders, front/EOF IFD) and cross-checked against tifffile; the observed StripOffsets histogram ({260:10, 262:55} expected) is logged, never assumed. Builds a uint16 9.36 um baseline (23x2832x2191, half-up convention pinned; uint16 legality verified in villa source - tifxyz_robust casts any dtype to float32 - plus a live probe with a pre-registered PLAN B uint8 fallback). Baseline inferred fwd+rev, scored on the native 3.24 um grid, GATED; then 12 rungs (pitch 4/5/6.5/8/12 via anti-aliased resample-to-P-then-regrid-to-9.36 so the model always runs at its trained pitch; 9.36 rung = baseline by construction; noise k*sigma_plate for k=1,2,4,8 with sigma_plate = adjacent-slice-MAD of the plate's own in-mask noise; uint16->uint8 released windowing; 3D blur sigma 1.0/2.0 px) in the gate-chosen direction. EXP B: fetches the three 500p2a windows (coords embedded; 3675 blosc chunks from the public HF bucket verified live, .zarray parsed and asserted; label counts asserted EXACT per window incl. win3's 621303 out-of-mask ink px, which are excluded from both classes) plus full-raster labels (byte sizes 3009475/2983168 asserted); runs ink_9um fwd AND rev on each window at 9.36 um (primary) and native 4.32 um (sensitivity), and on Frag1@9.36 (reuses baseline maps); scores every map vs real labels AND vs 40 rigidly translated label copies entirely inside (mask==1 AND label==0); reports the gap and pre-registered verdicts. Results as JSON to the served dir; previews as PNGs; idempotent per-stage markers + atomic zarr/pred writes; retry w/ 10/30/90 s backoff on all network ops; ALL DONE printed only after finalize re-verifies all 10 stage markers + all 29 preds + 4 results JSONs (refusal path tested, exit 3).
author.prereg_rules: EXP A (in header + out/prereg.json, locked at t~=3 s before any provisioning): scoring = exact tie-corrected pixel rank-AUC on the native 3.24 um grid, positives = ink&mask (5,339,364 px asserted), negatives = mask&~ink (23,803,476 px asserted), blank always (mask==1 AND label==0). BASELINE GATE: AUC_base = max(fwd,rev); if < 0.85 the ENTIRE run aborts as KILLED_BASELINE (justification: 0.85 keeps 0.35 of range above chance, the minimum that can order 13 rungs; an instrument that cannot read the undegraded plate supports no degradation claim). Rungs use the argmax direction (tie->forward). DETECTABLE <=> AUC_rung >= 0.75 AND retained = (AUC_rung-0.5)/(AUC_base-0.5) >= 0.50; detectability limit = coarsest DETECTABLE pitch. Noise = k*sigma_plate, k in {1,2,4,8} (SNR x 0.71/0.45/0.24/0.12 of the plate as scanned), seed 20260824, per-rung sub-seeded. Bit depth = rint(v/257) full-range released windowing (DEGENERATE-flagged under PLAN B). Blur sigma {1.0, 2.0} px. EXP B: primary scale = 9.36 um only (native 4.32 never verdict-bearing; 17 slices span 73 um there vs 159 trained). Audited cell = higher-real-AUC direction at primary scale. Null = 40 rigid translations of (label&mask), seed 20260824, |shift|_inf in [4.4 mm, 0.40*min(H,W)] (>= ~1.5-2 letter heights so translated strokes cannot overlap sources), each >= 50,000 pseudo-positive px; pos_i = T_i(shapes)&mask&~label, neg_i = mask&~label&~T_i(shapes). SHAPE-CONFOUNDED <=> median(40 null AUCs) >= 0.60 OR >= 20% of the 40 individually >= 0.60 (the OR-clause catches periodic text-row confounds that inflate the null max while leaving the median at/below 0.5 - demonstrated numerically pre-launch: synthetic row-confound gave median 0.44, max 0.96, 28% of draws >= 0.60; under a clean null 8/40 above 0.60 has ~zero probability). GENUINE <=> not confounded AND AUC_real > max of all 40 (rank p = 1/41 ~= 0.024; every positive beats a matched null) AND gap = AUC_real - median(null) >= 0.15; else INDETERMINATE. Data gates: all embedded label counts EXACT, window volume subsample stats within +-0.5 DN, Frag1 label sha256 equal to laptop ground truth - any miss => KILLED with evidence.
author.observability: status.txt exists and holds line L1 "BOOT pod_curve_audit v1 pid=... host=..." at t+0-1 s from script start (the 4th statement of the script, before any provisioning of any kind; script start = container start when used as the pod's start command). L2 at t+1-3 s: "SERVE http.server pid=... 0.0.0.0:8000 ... local_probe=200" - written only after a successful localhost curl of status.txt THROUGH the server (bound 0.0.0.0; external URL https://<POD_ID>-8000.proxy.runpod.net/status.txt printed in the line; the pod config must expose HTTP port 8000, stated in the launch header). L3 at t+2-4 s: "PREREG locked prereg.json sha256=..." - the decision rules are in the served dir before provisioning opens at t~=3-5 s. Measured in the local machinery run: all three lines landed within 1 s. HEARTBEAT every 60 s thereafter (first at ~t+60 s) with UTC timestamp, current stage, uptime, free disk; the heartbeat is also a watchdog that restarts a dead http server and logs SERVE RESTART - the specific failure that burned $2.30 on the zroll pod. Every stage opens/closes with === STAGE x OPEN/DONE (Ns) === lines; per-pass infer OPEN/DONE lines with elapsed; science lines (per-rung AUCs, per-cell gaps) stream into status.txt as they land. All stdout/stderr (tracebacks included) go to the served run.log. On failure: FATAL line with stage+line+command, FAILED marker, then an infinite lingering loop that keeps serving; ALL DONE is emitted only by the finalize stage after re-verifying the complete inventory (tested: injected failure produced exit 1 and zero ALL DONE lines).
author.cost_estimate: ~1.8-2.9 h wall on one RTX 5090 at the survey's $0.69-0.89/hr => ~$1.40-$2.60 (typical ~$2). Breakdown: provision 10-15 m, Frag1 6.7 GB 12-25 m, ckpt 1 m, baseline build+infer+gate 13-20 m, rung build+infer+score 25-40 m, p2a fetch 4-8 m, window build 6-10 m, window infer 25-40 m, scoring 6-12 m. NATIVE_WINDOWS=0 drops ~20-25 m (~$0.30). Early aborts are cheap and are results: ckpt/config or data-gate failure ~$0.35-0.60; KILLED_BASELINE ~$0.75-1.10. Disk: 100 GB volume recommended (villa env ~12 GB, TIFFs 6.7 GB, transient float32 memmaps peak ~11 GB, zarrs ~4 GB). Pod lingers serving results after ALL DONE and bills until Ben terminates it (stated in-band every 5 min; optional AUTOSTOP=1 stops the pod 30 min after ALL DONE via on-pod runpodctl - default off).
author.reviewer_findings: The adversarial pass changed five things, one of them load-bearing. (1) THE PREREG RULE ITSELF: a synthetic validation I built to attack my own null showed the median-only shape-confound threshold provably MISSES periodic confounds - a detector firing on text-ROW structure re-aligns only at shifts near multiples of the line spacing, giving null median 0.44 but null max 0.96 with 28% of draws >= 0.60. Added the pre-registered OR-clause (>= 20% of the 40 nulls >= 0.60 => SHAPE_CONFOUNDED) to header, prereg.json, and code, then re-validated: genuine detector => GENUINE (frac 0.00), periodic confound => SHAPE_CONFOUNDED (frac 0.28), neither misclassified. (2) 65*3.24/9.36 = 22.5 EXACTLY, and np.rint's half-even was FP-jitter fragile there (unit test caught it returning 23 via a 1e-15 error); replaced with an epsilon-guarded half-up convention, z-count pinned deterministically to 23. (3) Noise-rung RNG drew from one sequential stream with skip-on-exists, so a resumed run would generate DIFFERENT noise than a fresh run; switched to per-rung default_rng([SEED, k]). (4) finalize.py read direction.txt before its inventory check - a missing file tracebacked instead of producing the clean REFUSED listing; guarded (refusal path now tested, exit 3, lists all 31 expected artifacts). (5) Chunk missing-check could raise FileNotFoundError instead of reporting; made existence-safe. Validated-without-change: hist AUC exactly matches brute-force pairwise AUC with heavy ties (3 trials, <1e-12); translated-null histograms byte-match an explicit full-canvas shift reference; the banded two-pass resampler is band-size independent to the byte; failure injection, idempotent resume (10/10 stages skipped), and orphan-free cleanup all proven in foreground DRY runs.
author.problems: (1) Never executed end-to-end against the real pod/GPU: provisioning and inference invocations are inherited verbatim from the proven zroll/runbook recipes and every logic path was validated locally, but the first 15 min on the pod are the real test - watch for CKPT_CFG mode=flat crop=(17,128,128) and the FRAG1_VERIFY StripOffsets histogram {260:10, 262:55} before walking away. (2) The baseline gate is a live risk, by design: ink_9um has never been scored on Frag1 (scroll-trained model, fragment at 54 keV, resampled from 3.24 um); if max(fwd,rev) < 0.85 the run aborts as KILLED_BASELINE for ~$1 and that abort is the reported result per the standing rules - Ben should treat this as a plausible outcome, not a malfunction. (3) External-availability assumptions verified TODAY (2026-08-24) with tiny probes: dl.ash2txt.org serves Frag1 unauthenticated with exact byte fingerprints, and the HF 500p2a BUCKET (huggingface.co/buckets/..., not the 401-gated datasets/ namespace - probed both) is public; if either gate changes, the script fails loudly at the fetch stage with the URL in the log rather than proceeding on wrong data. (4) dl.ash2txt.org has rate-limited past sessions (429s); mitigated with 2.5 s sleeps, curl --retry, resume, and outer 10/30/90 backoff, but a hard block would stop the run (loudly, resumably). (5) Exp B native-4.32 cells are off-domain in z (model's 17 slices span 73 um vs 159 trained) - pre-registered as sensitivity-only and never verdict-bearing, but expect them to look worse than the primary cells. (6) The 0.85 gate, 0.60/20% confound thresholds, and 0.15 gap are justified but not calibrated against a prior run of this model on this plate (none exists); they are locked before data precisely so they cannot be tuned afterward, and all raw AUCs ship in the JSON for any explicitly-labeled post-hoc reanalysis.
